title: Lefse
subtitle: Norwegian soft potato flatbread
excerpt: Cooked mashed potato is mixed with flour and rolled into thin rounds, then cooked on a hot dry griddle until freckled. Lefse is a Norwegian soft flatbread eaten buttered or wrapped around fillings. Made in large batches before Christmas in every Norwegian home.
sourceNotes: Lefse is a Norwegian soft flatbread made from cooked potato. It is eaten buttered, rolled up, or used to wrap savoury fillings. Traditionally made in large batches before Christmas.

content.text: Lefse dough is delicate. The potato must be cold before you add the flour -- warm potato makes a sticky dough that tears when rolled. Chill the dough balls well before rolling and use a very generously floured surface.

items.prepNote: boiled, peeled, and mashed or riced

content.text: While potatoes are still warm, mix with butter, milk, and salt until smooth. Spread on a tray and leave to cool completely -- at least 30 minutes. Do not rush this step.
Add flour to the cold potato and mix to a soft dough. Divide into 10 equal balls. Chill for 30 minutes.
On a very well-floured surface, roll each ball out into a thin circle about 25cm wide -- aim for about 2mm thick.
Cook on a dry, very hot griddle or frying pan for 1-2 minutes per side until light brown spots appear.
Stack under a clean tea towel to keep soft.

items.cause: Dough too warm or too much flour added
items.fix: Chill the dough balls well before rolling and use a light touch on a generously floured surface.

content.text: Norway. Eaten buttered at Christmas, or wrapped around meat, potatoes, or brown cheese in everyday cooking. A source of real national pride, especially among Norwegian-American communities.
